retired_source_document.title: Report of the Auditor General on the Financial Statements of the National Government for FY 2023/2024

emphasis_of_matter: Debt service costs consuming 62.8% of ordinary revenue
Recurring nature of audit findings from previous years
basis_for_qualification: Unexplained Consolidated Fund balance differences of KES 156.8 billion
Incomplete government property register affecting asset valuation
Unresolved pending bills of KES 589.7 billion

delete_audits.finding_text: Accumulated pending bills of KES 589.7 billion remain unresolved across government ministries, departments and agencies, posing significant fiscal risk to ongoing service delivery
delete_audits.recommended_action: The National Treasury should develop a comprehensive pending bills clearance strategy with prioritized payment schedules

delete_audits.finding_text: Irregular procurement of medical supplies worth KES 12.3 billion without competitive bidding, including COVID-19 related emergency purchases that lacked proper documentation
delete_audits.recommended_action: Ministry should provide full documentation for emergency procurements and ensure future compliance with PPDA Act 2015

provenance.report_section: Ministry of Roads and Transport Vote

delete_audits.finding_text: Road construction project cost overruns totaling KES 47.8 billion across 23 major infrastructure projects, with some projects exceeding original estimates by over 200%
delete_audits.recommended_action: Implement project cost management controls and conduct forensic audits on projects with overruns exceeding 50%

delete_audits.finding_text: Expenditure amounting to KES 8.7 billion classified under 'classified operations' lacked verifiable supporting documentation accessible to the Auditor General
delete_audits.recommended_action: Establish secure audit arrangements for classified expenditure in line with Section 69 of the Public Finance Management Act

delete_audits.finding_text: Grants to secondary schools and TVET institutions totaling KES 6.2 billion disbursed without adequate confirmation of receipt or utilization reports from beneficiary institutions
delete_audits.recommended_action: Require mandatory utilization certificates before subsequent disbursements and conduct spot-check audits

delete_audits.finding_text: National debt service costs rose to KES 1.17 trillion (62.8% of ordinary revenue), threatening fiscal sustainability. External debt refinancing losses from currency depreciation amounted to KES 234 billion
delete_audits.recommended_action: Diversify debt portfolio towards longer-tenor concessional borrowing and establish hedging mechanisms for foreign currency exposure

delete_audits.finding_text: Ghost workers and irregular payroll entries costing KES 3.4 billion identified across National Police Service and Kenya Prisons Service payrolls
delete_audits.recommended_action: Conduct biometric verification of all uniformed services personnel and integrate IPPD with IPRS for real-time validation

delete_audits.finding_text: Fertilizer subsidy programme disbursed KES 9.1 billion with significant irregularities including payments to unregistered farmers and inflated pricing by contracted suppliers
delete_audits.recommended_action: Digitize farmer registration and implement e-voucher system to prevent diversion of subsidized inputs

delete_audits.finding_text: Kenya Pipeline Company and National Oil Corporation revenue remittances to the Exchequer fell short by KES 4.6 billion against projected targets, with unreconciled pipeline throughput fees
delete_audits.recommended_action: Automate revenue collection and remittance monitoring for all energy sector parastatals

delete_audits.finding_text: 14 water and irrigation projects worth KES 28.3 billion remained stalled or behind schedule, with accumulated idle costs and contractor claims totaling KES 5.7 billion
delete_audits.recommended_action: Establish project monitoring dashboards and enforce liquidated damages clauses for delayed contractors

delete_audits.finding_text: Huduma Namba and Integrated National Management System projects exceeded budget by KES 7.2 billion with incomplete deliverables and vendor lock-in concerns
delete_audits.recommended_action: Commission independent technology assessment and require open-standard compliance in all future ICT procurements

delete_audits.finding_text: 64 diplomatic missions had unexplained expenditure variances of KES 2.1 billion, with 12 missions failing to submit accounts for the entire fiscal year
delete_audits.recommended_action: Deploy unified financial management systems across all missions and require quarterly reporting compliance

delete_audits.finding_text: Government immovable property register remains incomplete — an estimated 40% of government-owned land parcels worth approximately KES 1.2 trillion lack updated title documentation
delete_audits.recommended_action: Fast-track the National Land Information Management System digitization and conduct nationwide verification of government properties

delete_audits.finding_text: Inua Jamii and cash transfer programmes had identified inclusion errors affecting 340,000 ineligible beneficiaries, with leakage estimated at KES 4.8 billion annually
delete_audits.recommended_action: Implement biometric authentication for all social protection disbursements and conduct beneficiary re-registration

delete_audits.finding_text: Correctional facilities across the country have accumulated a maintenance backlog costing KES 1.8 billion, with 28 facilities rated as structurally compromised
delete_audits.recommended_action: Develop a 5-year facility rehabilitation plan with allocated annual budget provisions

delete_audits.finding_text: National parks and game reserves revenue collection shortfall of KES 3.2 billion due to outdated collection systems and unmonitored entry points
delete_audits.recommended_action: Deploy electronic revenue collection at all park gates and automate reconciliation with KWS headquarters

delete_audits.finding_text: Youth Enterprise Development Fund and Sports Fund disbursements totaling KES 2.9 billion lacked proper beneficiary verification and recovery mechanisms for non-performing loans
delete_audits.recommended_action: Strengthen credit assessment processes and establish legal recovery framework for defaulting beneficiaries

delete_audits.finding_text: National Climate Change Action Plan funds of KES 1.4 billion had low absorption rates (32%) with significant funds returned to Treasury unspent
delete_audits.recommended_action: Build implementation capacity within the ministry and streamline climate fund disbursement procedures

provenance.report_section: Ministry of EAC and ASALs Vote

delete_audits.finding_text: ASAL development fund disbursements of KES 5.3 billion had inadequate monitoring and evaluation, with 60% of funded projects lacking completion reports
delete_audits.recommended_action: Establish integrated M&E framework and require project completion certificates before final payment tranches

delete_audits.finding_text: Mineral royalty collections fell short by KES 2.7 billion against estimated potential, with inadequate monitoring of mining operations and under-declared production volumes
delete_audits.recommended_action: Deploy real-time production monitoring systems at major mining sites and strengthen royalty audit capacity

delete_audits.finding_text: Hustler Fund and MSME development fund disbursements of KES 8.4 billion had repayment rates below 40%, threatening fund sustainability
delete_audits.recommended_action: Implement credit scoring for disbursements and integrate with CRB for defaulter tracking

delete_audits.finding_text: National Gender and Equality Commission programmes spent only KES 890 million of KES 2.1 billion allocation, with procurement delays and poor project implementation
delete_audits.recommended_action: Conduct capacity assessment and develop quarterly expenditure targets with management accountability

delete_audits.finding_text: The Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) had 847 override transactions worth KES 34.2 billion where standard controls were bypassed without adequate justification
delete_audits.recommended_action: Review and restrict override privileges, implement real-time monitoring of override transactions, and require dual authorization for all overrides above KES 10M

delete_audits.finding_text: Material differences of KES 156.8 billion between CBK records and National Treasury records for the Consolidated Fund remain unexplained as at end of FY 2023/24
delete_audits.recommended_action: Establish a dedicated reconciliation unit and complete monthly reconciliation with CBK within 30 days of period end

delete_audits.finding_text: The Auditor General issued a qualified opinion on the National Government financial statements for FY 2023/24, citing material misstatements in pending bills, payroll, and asset registers across multiple ministries
delete_audits.recommended_action: All accounting officers should address audit queries within the statutory 60-day response window and implement previous audit recommendations
